title: Station food and ekiben
intro: Ekiben (駅弁, eki = station + bentō) is the regional lunch box sold for eating on the train. Every line has its own: Yonezawa beef rice, the clay pot of Yokokawa, Toyama's trout sushi. Buying the right ekiben before the shinkansen is half the fun of a train day.

Big Japanese stations are food halls too: ramen streets, souvenir sweets, standing soba on the platform. This guide covers what to buy and where on our own train days, and how the seven of us, Fernanda included, eat well on them.
Prices and hours marked "verified" were checked on an official site or a Japanese source in Oct 2026; everything else is "to confirm".

sections.title: Our train days
sections.body: Six legs, and what to eat on each. Buy at the departure station, 20–30 minutes before the train. On shinkansen and limited expresses with reserved seats, eating is normal; on local trains with bench seats along the sides, wait.

items.name: Thu 24 Dec · Tokyo → Nagano (Hokuriku shinkansen)
items.what: The best start there is: Tokyo Station's Ekiben-ya Matsuri (150+ ekiben from all over Japan) and GranSta, both inside the gates, or Daimaru's bento street just outside. This is the line of Tōge no Kamameshi (Ogino-ya, from Yokokawa and Karuizawa), 2025's top ekiben.
items.where: Tokyo Station (GranSta, Ekiben-ya Matsuri, Daimaru B1); ecute Ueno if we board at Ueno
items.tip: Matsuri opens 05:30. Christmas Eve is busy at the depachika, so buy early.

items.name: Sun 27 Dec · Nagano → Kanazawa (Hokuriku shinkansen)
items.what: Nagano Station's MIDORI: oyaki, Shinshū soba, miso and the prefecture's sake. Further down the line, Toyama is masu-no-sushi country (Minamoto sells it at Toyama and Shin-Takaoka stations), but we don't get off there.
items.tip: MIDORI hours to confirm. Masu no sushi often turns up at Tokyo's Matsuri; it's cured trout, so not for Fernanda.

items.name: Wed 30 Dec · Kanazawa → Kyoto (shinkansen to Tsuruga, then Thunderbird)
items.what: Kanazawa Station's Anto, right by the gates: Kaga sweets, leaf-wrapped pressed sushi (笹寿司), sake and ekiben. すゞめ in the station's Hyakubangai is on Tabelog's 2026 wagashi list. Fukui's crab-rice ekiben (Echizen Kanimeshi) comes from Fukui Station, which the shinkansen passes on the way to Tsuruga.
items.tip: Many Anto shops 8:30–20:00 (to confirm). 28–30 Dec is the peak for trains out of the cities: reserve seats early. The Thunderbird is a reserved-seat limited express, so eating on board is fine.

items.name: Tue 5 Jan · Kyoto → Kawaguchiko (via Mishima/Shizuoka or Tokyo)
items.what: Stock up at Kyoto Station before the Tōkaidō shinkansen: JR Kyoto Isetan's B1 has a corner of bentō from old, famous houses and an Izuu counter (saba-zushi, 3.57). Kyoto Ramen Kōji (10F) and Honke Daiichi Asahi by the station (opens 6:00) cover a hot meal. We have no researched station food for Mishima or Shizuoka; if we change in Tokyo, GranSta is on the way.
items.where: Kyoto Station · JR Kyoto Isetan B1
items.tip: JR Central stopped on-board food sales on the Tōkaidō in 2023: buy before boarding. Kaki no ha zushi and Izuu's mackerel are cured fish, so Fernanda takes a cooked bentō.

items.name: Thu 7 Jan · Kawaguchiko → Tokyo
items.what: No station hall worth the name in our research. Eat lunch in town (Kiji-tei, 10 min walk from Kawaguchiko Station, is open on Thursdays) and take konbini tea and snacks for the ride.
items.tip: If it's a train with bench seats along the sides, wait until Tokyo to eat.

items.name: Sat 9 Jan · Tokyo, departure
items.what: The last ekiben: Ekiben-ya Matsuri (05:30–22:00) or Daimaru's bento street, and sake at Hasegawa Saketen in GranSta.
items.tip: A three-day weekend starts on the 9th: allow 30 minutes for the Matsuri queue.

sections.title: A bit of history
sections.body:
The official date is 16 July 1885: the day Nippon Railway opened Utsunomiya Station, the Shirakiya inn (白木屋) sold two rice balls with takuan wrapped in bamboo leaf. That's why 16 July is Ekiben Day (駅弁記念日). The claim is disputed: Japanese Wikipedia lists earlier ones at Umeda and Kobe (~1877), Kumagaya and Ueno (1883), and Tsuruga and Takasaki (1884). The multi-dish boxed bentō (the "makunouchi") is credited to Maneki of Himeji in 1889/1890.

Long steam journeys with long stops made the golden age: platform vendors (立ち売り) with trays round their necks and tea in little clay pots (汽車土瓶). Before the war, army orders for troops in transit made the makers grow; in 1943 rationing swapped rice for sweet potato. After the war, department-store ekiben fairs (Takashimaya Osaka in 1953; Keiō Shinjuku's famous one every January since 1966) made regional ekiben known nationwide.

Speed brought the decline: the shinkansen barely stops, windows don't open, and konbini compete. By 2016 fewer than ten stations still had platform vendors, and the on-board trolley kept shrinking (JR Central ended food sales on the Tōkaidō in 2023; other lines to confirm). Today you buy your ekiben before boarding, and the station shops gather them from all over Japan.

sections.title: Manners: where you can eat
sections.body:
Shinkansen and limited expresses with reserved seats (forward-facing seats with a tray table): eating is allowed and expected. Nobody minds seven people opening lunch boxes, or a beer.

Subways and local trains with bench seats along the sides (like the Yamanote): don't eat. It isn't illegal, but it's frowned on; a bottle of water is fine. Also avoid eating while walking in the street or along station corridors: eat standing by the vending machine or kiosk where you bought it.

Smell: very strong food (garlicky fried things, hot curry) bothers a full carriage. Cold rice classics and self-heating boxes are fine. Rubbish: collect everything in the shop's bag and use the bins in the shinkansen vestibules or on the platform, separating PET bottles and cans. Leave nothing on the seat.

sections.title: How to buy: timing, sell-outs and self-heating boxes
sections.body:
Buy at the departure station, 20–30 minutes before the train: the big shops sit inside the gates, near the shinkansen platforms. The famous ekiben come in limited batches and can sell out; if you want a particular one, go early (Getnavi says 「早めに」). On holidays and the New Year return, the Ekiben-ya Matsuri queue is long: allow 30 minutes.

Ekiben are made to be eaten cold (seasoned rice, nothing that spoils fast). The exceptions are self-heating boxes (加熱式): you pull a cord on the box, water meets quicklime (生石灰) in the base, and the reaction steams the food hot. It takes about 5–10 minutes (Travel Watch says ~10). Pull the cord with the box flat on the tray and the lid closed, and leave it alone: the bottom gets hot and steam comes out. The technology dates from 1988 (Awajiya, Kobe), and the famous ones are Sendai gyūtan and Kobe sukiyaki. They can't go on a plane.

Pay with Suica, card or cash. For a guaranteed pickup in Tokyo, JR East takes orders through 「ネットでエキナカ」 for collection at Ekiben-ya Odori (year-end availability to confirm).

sections.title: Tokyo Station: Japan's biggest buffet
sections.body: Three of our train days start or end here (24 Dec, 7 Jan, 9 Jan). Everything below is a few minutes from the shinkansen gates.

items.name: Ekiben-ya Matsuri
items.name_ja: 駅弁屋 祭 グランスタ東京
items.what: The temple: 150+ ekiben from all over Japan every day, plus Tokyo exclusives. Sales ranking (Jan–Jun 2024): 1) 牛肉どまん中, 2) チキン弁当, 3) 炭火焼風牛たん弁当, 4) まぐろいくら弁当, 5) 牛すきと牛焼肉弁当, 6) 深川めし, 7) えんがわ押し寿司, 8) 仙台名物牛たん弁当 (self-heating), 9) とりめし, 10) えび千両ちらし.
items.where: Inside the gates, GranSta Tokyo 1F, Central Passage, between the stairs to platforms 5/6 and 7/8
items.tip: Open 05:30–22:00 every day, no fixed closing day (verified, JR East, Feb 2026). Best time: early morning (6:00–9:00) for the full range and short queues. If it's packed, Ekiben-ya Odori (駅弁屋 踊, 6:00–21:00) next door sells the Matsuri's top 10.

items.name: GranSta Tokyo
items.what: A mall inside the gates (1F and B1) of designer bentō and delis. Highlights: Kiyōken (崎陽軒, shūmai), Asakusa Imahan (浅草今半, sukiyaki bentō), Date no Gyūtan (伊達の牛たん本舗), Maisen (とんかつ まい泉, tonkatsu sandwich), Yabaton (矢場とん), ONI&Co. (onigiri), Jiraiya (天むす 地雷也).
items.where: Inside the gates, Central Passage / B1
items.tip: Bentō and sweets: Mon–Sat 8:00–22:00, Sun and holidays 8:00–21:00 (verified, GranSta site, Oct 2026). Hours can change over long holidays.

items.name: GranSta Yaesu
items.what: Outside the gates on the Yaesu side: sit-down restaurants (Rikyū gyūtan, Yabaton tonkatsu, Tsukiji Sushisei, tempura, unagi). Good for a calm lunch before the train.
items.tip: Restaurants 11:00–22:00 (verified, GranSta site, Oct 2026).

items.name: Tokyo Ramen Street
items.name_ja: 東京ラーメンストリート
items.what: A corridor of famous Tokyo ramen shops in the basement of Tokyo Station Ichibangai. Long lunchtime queues; Rokurinsha's tsukemen is the most famous line.
items.where: Tokyo Station Ichibangai B1, Yaesu side (outside the gates)
items.tip: For seven, go at 10:30 or after 14:00 and expect to split. Shop list and hours to confirm on the Ichibangai site.

items.name: Tokyo Character Street and Tokyo Okashi Land
items.name_ja: 東京キャラクターストリート / 東京おかしランド
items.what: Side by side in Ichibangai B1. Character Street: TV and character shops (Pokémon, Ghibli, Hello Kitty). Okashi Land: Calbee, Glico and Morinaga with freshly made snacks and Tokyo-only editions.
items.where: Tokyo Station Ichibangai B1 (outside the gates)
items.tip: Good for the parents while the rest queue for ramen. Hours to confirm.

items.name: Kitchen Street and Nippon Gourmet Kaidō
items.name_ja: キッチンストリート / にっぽんグルメ街道
items.what: Kitchen Street is the row of restaurants on the Yaesu side (1F/B1); current line-up to confirm. Nippon Gourmet Kaidō (Ichibangai B1) gathers regional dishes.
items.tip: Plan B if Ramen Street's queue is long.

sections.title: The stations on our route
sections.body: At each one, look first for the shops inside the gates: buy and board.

items.name: Nagano: MIDORI
items.what: The station mall: oyaki, Shinshū soba, miso and the prefecture's sake. Our stop for the 27 Dec train to Kanazawa.
items.tip: Hours to confirm.

items.name: Kanazawa: Anto
items.name_ja: 金沢百番街 あんと
items.what: Kanazawa's souvenir and food arcade right by the gates: Kaga sweets, leaf-wrapped pressed sushi (笹寿司), sake, ekiben. Our stop for the 30 Dec train to Kyoto.
items.tip: Many shops 8:30–20:00 (to confirm); year-end hours to confirm.

items.name: Kyoto Station
items.what: Kyoto Ramen Kōji (京都拉麺小路) on 10F, with 10 shops from all over Japan (Toyama Black Iroha, Hakata Daruma, Menshō Takamatsu…). JR Kyoto Isetan has a strong B1 food hall for bentō and Kyoto sweets. Porta is the underground mall with simple restaurants. Shinpuku Saikan and Daiichi Asahi, the Kyoto ramen pair that sit side by side, are a few minutes' walk away. Our stop for the 5 Jan train.
items.where: Kyoto Station (Ramen Kōji: 10F, south of the big staircase)
items.tip: Ramen Kōji 11:00–22:00, last order 21:30 (verified, official site, Oct 2026); New Year to confirm. Daiichi Asahi opens 6:00 and closes Thursdays; Shinpuku Saikan closes Wednesdays.

items.name: ecute Ueno
items.what: The in-station mall for the Tōhoku, Jōetsu and Hokuriku lines at Ueno: bentō, delis and panda-themed sweets. Useful if we board the Nagano train at Ueno.
items.tip: Bentō 9:00–21:00 (Fri to 22:00) (verified, ecute site, Oct 2026).

items.name: ecute Shinagawa
items.what: In-station delis, bakery and sweets (Waraku Beniya, Atelier Ukai), for anyone boarding the Tōkaidō at Shinagawa. On the Yamanote platform is Tokiwaken (常盤軒), platform soba since 1964.
items.tip: Sweets 8:00–22:00 Mon–Sat, 8:00–20:30 Sun and holidays (verified, ecute site, Oct 2026).

sections.title: Elsewhere (only on an alternative route)
sections.body: Not on our plan, kept for the alternatives.

items.name: Shin-Osaka and Osaka/Umeda
items.name_ja: エキマルシェ新大阪 / 大阪駅
items.what: Eki Marché Shin-Osaka sits inside the conventional-line gates, with Osaka ekiben, sweets and restaurants. In Umeda, Eki Marché Osaka (82 shops, outside the gates) and Hanshin's food hall, which even sells Himeji's ekisoba.
items.tip: For the shinkansen, buy at Shin-Osaka; hours to confirm.

items.name: Hakata
items.what: Ming (マイング) is the ground-floor souvenir street (mentaiko, Hakata Tōrimon). Deitos and AMU Plaza have ramen and restaurants; the Kūten food floor is on AMU's 9F.
items.tip: Hours and New Year to confirm.

items.name: Sendai: Gyūtan-dōri, Sushi-dōri and Zunda Kōmichi
items.name_ja: 牛たん通り / すし通り / ずんだ小径
items.what: On the station's 3F: corridors of beef-tongue and sushi restaurants, and Zunda Saryō (ずんだ茶寮, by Kashō Sanzen) with its zunda shake: vanilla milkshake with sweet edamame paste.
items.where: Sendai Station, 3F, near the central shinkansen gate
items.tip: Zunda Saryō: shop 9:00–21:00, café 10:00–18:00 (secondary source, to confirm).

sections.title: Ekiben worth hunting, by line
sections.body: Checked against JR East's yearly passenger vote 「駅弁味の陣」 and the Ekiben-ya Matsuri sales ranking. Many of these are also sold at Tokyo's Matsuri, but the regional ones aren't there every day. Ours first.

items.name: Tōge no Kamameshi
items.what: Seasoned rice in a little Mashiko clay pot with chicken, mushroom, chestnut, quail egg and bamboo shoot, all cooked. Sold at Yokokawa, at the foot of the old Usui pass, since 1958. 2025 winner of 駅弁味の陣 (駅弁大将軍). You keep the pot.
items.where: Ogino-ya (荻野屋): Yokokawa, Karuizawa, shops in Tokyo (GINZA SIX) — our Hokuriku shinkansen line, 24 Dec
items.tip: The pot is heavy: one per couple is plenty if the bags are full.

items.name: Masu no Sushi
items.what: Pressed trout sushi in bamboo leaves, in a wooden round you cut like a pizza. Minamoto (源) has made it in Toyama since 1912. Its 「ますのすし劔」 won the Matsuri's special prize at 駅弁味の陣 2025.
items.where: Minamoto, Toyama and Shin-Takaoka stations (our 27 Dec line, but we don't stop); often at the Matsuri
items.tip: The trout is cured in salt and vinegar, not cooked: Fernanda skips it; the rest share a round.

items.name: Echizen Kanimeshi
items.what: Rice cooked in crab stock and crab roe, topped with shredded crab. An ekiben since 1961 (Banshō Honten, Fukui).
items.where: Banshō Honten (番匠本店), Fukui Station, on our 30 Dec line to Tsuruga

items.name: Kaki no Ha Zushi
items.what: Pressed sushi of cured mackerel or salmon wrapped in a persimmon leaf, from Nara and Wakayama.
items.where: Hiraso (平宗) and others: Nara, Kyoto and Shin-Osaka stations
items.tip: Cured fish, not cooked: Fernanda avoids it.

items.name: Fukagawa-meshi
items.what: Rice cooked with clams (asari) and burdock, a Fukagawa (Tokyo) fishermen's dish. The clams are well cooked. No. 6 in Matsuri sales; the frozen version won a prize at 駅弁味の陣 2025.
items.where: Nihonbashi Daimasu (日本ばし大増) at the Matsuri; a JR Central version in the Tōkaidō shinkansen shops (our 5 Jan line)

items.name: Gyūniku Domannaka
items.what: Yamagata Tsuyahime rice topped with beef simmered gyūdon-style. Launched in 1992 with the Yamagata shinkansen; No. 1 in Matsuri sales and winner of 駅弁味の陣 2024 (shio version).
items.where: Shinkineya (新杵屋), Yonezawa; also Ekiben-ya Matsuri, Tokyo

items.name: Shūmai Bentō
items.what: Yokohama's cult classic since 1954: 5 pork shūmai with dried scallop, rice in little cylinders with umeboshi, grilled tuna, karaage, tamagoyaki, bamboo shoot, and an apricot everyone argues about when to eat.
items.where: Kiyōken (崎陽軒): Yokohama, Shin-Yokohama, GranSta Tokyo B1 and many Kantō stations
items.tip: The best value on the list; it sells hard over New Year.

items.name: Chicken Bentō
items.what: A Tokyo classic since 1964: karaage and ketchup rice. No. 2 in Matsuri sales. Good for anyone who doesn't want fish.
items.where: Ekiben-ya Matsuri, Tokyo (JR East Cross Station)

items.name: Self-heating gyūtan bentō
items.name_ja: 仙台名物 牛たん弁当 (加熱式)
items.what: Thick slices of grilled beef tongue on rice, with a heating cord. No. 8 in Matsuri sales. There's also an unheated version, 炭火焼風牛たん弁当 (No. 3).
items.where: Kobayashi (こばやし) and others, Sendai; Ekiben-ya Matsuri
items.price: ~¥1,580 in 2021 (to confirm; tongue prices have risen a lot)
items.tip: The meat comes well done. Pull the cord and wait ~10 min.

items.name: Torimeshi (Ōdate)
items.what: Rice cooked in chicken stock with sweet-savoury chicken on top, created in 1947. Two-time winner of 駅弁味の陣 (2015, 2016) and winner again in 2023.
items.where: Hanazen (花善), Ōdate Station (Akita); sometimes at the Matsuri

items.name: Hipparidako-meshi
items.what: Simmered octopus and anago on seasoned rice in a clay pot shaped like an octopus trap. Created in 1998 for the Akashi Kaikyō bridge.
items.where: Awajiya (淡路屋): Nishi-Akashi, Shin-Kobe, Shin-Osaka; sometimes in Tokyo

items.name: Acchicchi Tajima-gyū Sukiyaki Bentō
items.name_ja: あっちっち但馬牛すき焼き弁当
items.what: Self-heating sukiyaki of Tajima beef (Awajiya, who invented the system). It comes with a pasteurised raw egg for dipping.
items.tip: Fernanda eats the beef and leaves the raw egg.

items.name: Kashiwa-meshi
items.what: Rice cooked in chicken stock topped with shredded chicken, egg and strips of nori. A Kyushu classic from Tōchikuken (東筑軒), sold at Orio, Kokura and Hakata.

items.name: Engawa Oshizushi
items.what: Pressed sushi of marinated flounder fin (Kamio Bentō, Niigata). No. 7 in Matsuri sales.
items.tip: Marinated or seared raw fish: Fernanda skips it.

items.name: Maguro Ikura Bentō
items.what: Marinated tuna and salmon roe on sushi rice. No. 4 in Matsuri sales.
items.pregnancy_note: Raw fish: for Fernanda, swap it for Domannaka, the Shūmai Bentō or Fukagawa-meshi.
items.tip: For Fernanda, swap it for Domannaka, the Shūmai Bentō or Fukagawa-meshi.

sections.title: Station food that isn't ekiben
sections.body: Tachigui (立ち食い) soba and udon: a standing counter, a ticket from the machine, a bowl in 3 minutes. It's the Japanese office worker's meal, and many are very good.

items.name: Kitsune udon in Kansai
items.what: In Kyoto and Osaka, station udon comes in a clear kombu-and-katsuobushi broth with sweet fried tofu. Any platform counter in Kyoto or Shin-Osaka does it well.
items.where: Udon counters on Kansai platforms (Kyoto on 5 Jan)

items.name: Station ramen
items.what: Tokyo Ramen Street (Tokyo) and Kyoto Ramen Kōji (Kyoto 10F) gather well-known shops; in Hakata, tonkotsu ramen at Deitos/AMU.

items.name: Station kissaten
items.what: Old-style cafés with a morning set (thick toast, boiled egg, coffee). Good for the parents while we wait for a train. Ask for "mōningu".

items.name: Nadai Fuji Soba
items.what: Tokyo's cheap soba chain, open late (many 24 hours). Honest verdict: a decent quick meal, not a pilgrimage. Insurance when everything else is shut.

items.name: Tokiwaken (Shinagawa)
items.what: Platform soba since 1964, from a house that has sold ekiben at Shinagawa since 1922. House dish: the "Shinagawa-don". Two counters: the Yamanote and Yokosuka platforms.
items.tip: Yamanote: 6:00–23:30 (Norimono News, 2021; to confirm).

items.name: Himeji ekisoba
items.what: Since 19 Oct 1949: yellow Chinese noodles (with kansui) in Japanese dashi, born of the post-war shortage of good udon flour. A dish that exists only there. Not on our route.
items.where: Maneki (まねき食品): kiosks on the Sanyō line platforms and Maneki Dining by the shinkansen gate; also Hanshin's food hall in Umeda
items.tip: Platforms 5/6 and 7/8.

sections.title: Omiyage: sweets to take home
sections.body: Omiyage is the compulsory travel gift: you bring regional sweets back for colleagues and family, individually wrapped for sharing. Stations sell each city's icons.

items.name: Nama Yatsuhashi
items.what: Soft cinnamon rice dough folded over bean paste: the Kyoto sweet.

items.name: Tokyo Banana
items.what: Banana-shaped sponge with banana cream, by Grapestone, since 1991. For years the best-selling sweet at Tokyo Station. Honest verdict: soft, sweet and bland; it's about the packaging.

items.name: Gin no Budō
items.what: Grapestone's smarter sweets label (Sugar Butter Tree and the like).

items.name: Funawa imo-yōkan
items.what: A sweet-potato bar made with just sugar and salt, from Asakusa since 1902. Simple and honest.

items.name: Akafuku
items.what: Mochi under waves of bean paste, from Ise (since 1707). Keeps 2–3 days: buy it close to eating.

items.name: Hagi no Tsuki
items.what: Round sponge filled with custard, from Sendai's Kashō Sanzen (1979). Perhaps the best omiyage in Japan. Not on our route.

items.name: Momiji Manjū
items.what: Maple-leaf cakes from Miyajima/Hiroshima, for the Hiroshima alternative.

items.name: Hakata Tōrimon
items.what: A buttery manjū filled with white bean and milk, from Fukuoka's Meigetsudō. Excellent. Not on our route.

items.name: Shiroi Koibito
items.what: Hokkaido white-chocolate biscuits. Skip: not on our route, and there are better choices.

sections.title: A shinkansen lunch for seven
sections.body:
Buy seven different ekiben and share: that's how you taste the most. A safe spread for Fernanda (all cooked): 牛肉どまん中, シウマイ弁当, 峠の釜めし, 深川めし, 鶏めし or かしわめし, and a self-heating gyūtan. If some want sushi, they share a ますのすし or 柿の葉寿司; she doesn't. For her, skip any ekiben with raw fish, roe, raw egg (the sukiyaki dip) or anything "rare".

Add green tea or hōjicha in a bottle (konbini), some fruit, and a local sweet for dessert. Give her an aisle seat near the toilet. If the train leaves after lunch, buy in the morning and keep it out of the sun: ekiben keep at room temperature for a few hours (the time is on the label).

sections.title: Year-end and New Year
sections.body:
Stations run over New Year and trains fill up: 28–30 Dec (out of the cities) and 2–4 Jan (back). Our 30 Dec Kanazawa → Kyoto leg is right in the outbound rush, so reserve seats early.

Ekiben-ya Matsuri opens every day with no fixed closing day, 05:30–22:00 (verified, JR East, 2026); hours for 31 Dec and 1 Jan were not published. GranSta warns that hours change over long holidays. Smaller regional shops and makers may close on 1 Jan or sell a reduced range. On busy travel days, arrive 30–40 minutes before the train and have a plan B (the station konbini, always open).

In January, Keiō Shinjuku holds its big ekiben fair (since 1966; 2027 dates to confirm): if it overlaps our 7–8 Jan in Tokyo, it's worth the trip.
